subtopics.title: Inside the Atom — Protons, Neutrons and Electrons

questions.question: The gold-foil experiment proved that:
options: Atoms are soft balls of spread-out positive charge
Nearly all the atom's mass and all its positive charge sit in a tiny central nucleus
Gold atoms are heavier than most

questions.question: The three particles' charges and relative masses are:
options: Proton +1 mass 1; neutron 0 mass 0; electron -1 mass 1
Proton 0 mass 1; neutron +1 mass 1; electron -1 tiny
Proton +1 mass 1; neutron 0 mass 1; electron -1 with about one two-thousandth of a proton's mass
All three carry charge and equal mass

questions.question: In the stadium picture, the pea on the centre spot represents:
options: The nucleus — nearly all the mass in a tiny fraction of the space

questions.question: A neutral atom has:
options: Equal numbers of protons and neutrons always
Equal numbers of protons and electrons, so the charges cancel exactly

subtopics.title: Atomic Number, Mass Number, Notation and Ions

questions.question: The atomic number Z is:
options: The number of protons — the element's identity

questions.question: Aluminium twenty-seven, with Z equal to 13, contains:
options: 13 protons, 14 neutrons and, when neutral, 13 electrons

questions.question: Ions form when atoms:
options: Gain or lose electrons — never protons

questions.question: Mg two-plus and O two-minus carry, respectively:
options: Two extra protons and two missing protons
10 electrons each — magnesium lost two, oxygen gained two

questions.question: Isotopes of an element have:
options: Different proton counts and identical neutron counts
The same proton count but different neutron counts, so different mass numbers

questions.question: Isotopes are chemically identical because:
options: Chemistry is run by the electrons, and both isotopes carry identical electron arrangements
They always occur in equal amounts

questions.question: With 20 percent boron-10 and 80 percent boron-11, the relative atomic mass is:
An average of 10,8 sitting close to 11 tells you at a glance that:
options: No boron atom exists at all
The heavier isotope dominates the natural mixture

subtopics.title: Energy Levels, Orbitals and Electron Configuration

questions.question: An orbital is:
options: A fixed circular track around the nucleus
A region of space where an electron is most likely found, holding at most two electrons
Another name for an energy level

questions.question: The filling order for elements up to Z equal to 20 is:
Hund's rule says that in a set of equal-energy p orbitals:
options: Electrons spread out singly before any pairing — phosphorus parks one in each 3p orbital
Electrons pair up immediately in the first orbital
Only one orbital may ever be used
Electrons skip to the next level instead

questions.question: Aluminium's sp notation, checked against Z, is:
In the inflated-atom stadium, the stands are:
options: The electrons' territory — almost completely empty space

questions.question: The electrons stay in the stands because:
options: The stadium walls hold them in
They are too heavy to leave
The positive pea attracts every negative electron — opposite charges attract

questions.question: The rare hard bounce-backs in the foil experiment showed that:
options: Something tiny, dense and charged sits at the atom's centre — the pea is real

questions.question: In the twins picture, the backpacks are:
options: The neutrons — extra neutrons add mass without changing behaviour

questions.question: Boron-10 and boron-11 share:
options: Five protons and identical chemistry — only their masses differ

questions.question: Worked the school-marks way, boron's 10,8 comes from:
options: Averaging 10 and 11 to get 10,5 and rounding up
20 hundredths of 10 — which is 2 — plus 80 hundredths of 11 — which is 8,8

subtopics.title: Filling the Hotel From the Ground Floor

questions.question: The hotel's rule one says electrons:
options: Always take the cheapest available room — lowest energy first

questions.question: The famous quirk in the filling order is that:
options: The p rooms fill before the s rooms
The 4s room is slightly cheaper than the remaining floor-3 rooms, so 4s fills next

questions.question: The free self-check on any register is:
options: The last superscript must always be two
Adding the superscripts must recover the element's atomic number
Every floor must be completely full
